title: Platform systems & services: dashboards, alerts, runbooks, roadmap and retrospective (2026 Q4)
author: Ava Chen
content:
Overview:
This document consolidates the Platform team's canonical guidance for systems and services inventory, recommended dashboards and alert thresholds, operational runbooks for high-severity events, the Q4 2026 roadmap items affecting platform reliability, and a short retrospective of runbook/alerting improvements deployed in the last two quarters. Target audience: on-call SREs, platform engineers, product owners who depend on platform SLAs.

Scope and intent:
- Scope: components owned by Platform (control-plane, routing-service, autoscaler, batcher, cache-service, observability stack).
- Intent: provide a single reference for (1) where to find dashboards, (2) what alerts mean and how to react, (3) runbook procedures for common failures, and (4) planned changes and owners.

1) Systems & services inventory (summary)
Service | Owner | On-call rotation | Primary metrics
- control-plane-api | Platform-API team (owner: Marcus Patel) | platform-api-rotation | uptime, p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate
- routing-service | Serving Runtime team (owner: Leila Gomez) | serving-routing-rotation | request_latency_ms, error_rate, fallback_count, model_variant_fallbacks
- autoscaler | Platform Infra (owner: Sanjay Rao) | infra-autoscaler-rotation | scale_events_per_min, scale_latency, pending_work_items
- batcher | Serving Runtime (owner: Priya Nair) | serving-batcher-rotation | batch_size_avg, throughput_tps, cold_start_rate
- kv-cache | Platform Cache (owner: Omar Diaz) | cache-rotation | hit_ratio, eviction_rate, memory_used_bytes
- observability | Observability team (owner: Jenna Park) | obs-rotation | ingestion_rate, alert_count, prometheus_remote_write_failures

2) SLOs and alerting thresholds (production defaults)
- Control-plane API
  - SLO: 99.9% availability monthly (target), p95 latency < 150ms, p99 < 400ms.
  - Alert: control_plane_5xx_rate > 0.1% sustained for 5 minutes (sev-2).
  - Alert: control_plane_p99_latency > 500ms for 10m (sev-2).

- Routing / Serving
  - SLO: request success rate 99.5% (business-critical models), p95 latency < 200ms.
  - Alert: serving_request_error_rate > 0.5% for 5m (sev-1 if rising and customer impact detected).
  - Alert: model_variant_fallback_rate > 2% for 15m (investigate compatibility/throughput).

- Batcher & KV-cache
  - SLO: batcher throughput degradation < 20% vs baseline; kv-cache hit_ratio >= 85% for workloads with caching enabled.
  - Alert: batcher_batch_size_drop > 40% for 10m (sev-2).
  - Alert: kv_cache_hit_ratio < 60% for 15m (sev-2).

- GPU fleet (Dedicated/Private)
  - SLO: node_health >= 99.0% and GPU_utilization between 40-85% for cost-effectiveness.
  - Alert: gpu_node_offline_count > 1 for pool with < 10 nodes (sev-1).

3) Recommended dashboards (location: Grafana -> org: platform -> folder: Platform — Live)
Important panels (panel name and metrics):
- "Cluster overview" — node_count, gpu_available_count, avg_gpu_utilization
- "Serving latency breakdown" — infra.request_latency_ms p50/p95/p99, split by model-type and region
- "Error summary" — 5xx rate by service, recent incidents overlay
- "Batcher health" — batch_size_avg, throughput_tps, queue_length
- "KV cache" — hit_ratio, eviction_rate, memory_used_bytes by cache shard
- "Autoscaler activity" — scale_events_per_min, scale_latency, pending_work_items
- "Cost & token breakdown" — tokens_generated_by_model, token_cost_usd_by_model (used for capacity decisions)

Example PromQL snippets used in panels (copy to Grafana Prometheus datasource)
- p95 request latency (ms) for routing-service: 
  sum by (instance) (histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(infra_http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="routing-service"}[5m]))) * 1000

- 5xx error rate (1m): 
  sum(rate(infra_http_requests_total{job="routing-service",status=~"5.."}[1m])) / sum(rate(infra_http_requests_total{job="routing-service"}[1m]))

- KV cache hit ratio: 
  sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) / (sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) + sum(rate(kv_cache_misses_total[5m])))

4) Runbooks (prioritized, with owner and runbook steps)
Note: always page the on-call rotation for the service (PagerDuty) as first step on high-sev alerts.

Runbook: High 5xx rate on routing-service (sev-1 escalation)
1) Acknowledge the alert in PagerDuty and open the incident channel (#inc-serving-routing).
2) Check dashboards: serving latency breakdown, error summary, and recent deploys (CI/CD).
3) Run quick health checks: curl -s -w "%{http_code}" -o /dev/null https://routing-service.internal/healthz on a control-plane host.
4) If errors correlate with a recent deploy (last 30m), roll back to the previous revision: 
   - CI: ping the deployment manager -> look for job "routing-deploy".
   - Command (example): kubectl -n platform rollout undo deployment/routing-service --to-revision=<previous>
5) If errors correlate with high GPU OOMs or memory pressure, check node metrics and coordinate with infra-autoscaler to drain affected nodes.
6) If none of the above: increase log-level to DEBUG for 10m to capture traces, gather stack traces, and escalate to Serving Runtime leads.
7) Post-incident: attach timeline and root cause to the incident ticket and schedule a follow-up RCA within 3 business days.

Runbook: KV cache eviction storm (sev-2)
1) Verify eviction_rate vs memory_used_bytes on cache shard panels.
2) If eviction_rate high and memory near limit, scale cache pool: terraform apply -var='shard=cache-shard-<id> scale_delta=+2' OR use internal cache scaling API: POST /api/v1/cache/shards/<id>/scale {"delta":2}.
3) Temporarily enable spill-to-disk if configured and notify affected customers.
4) Backfill cache if necessary using cache-warmup job (cronjob name: cache-warmup-shard-<id>).

Runbook: Autoscaler not scaling (sev-1)
1) Check autoscaler logs and scale_events_per_min panel.
2) Validate control-plane connectivity to cloud APIs (cloud-accounts-and-networking playbook).
3) If cloud API rate-limited: contact Cloud Provider ops and execute pre-approved escalation template.
4) As a mitigation, manually scale target pools via infra-runbooks: terraform apply or cloud console.

5) Retrospective summary (last two quarters)
What we observed:
- Several incidents were caused by under-specified alerts (p99 thresholds too conservative) which led to noisy paging.
- Batcher performance regressions correlated with a single poorly-performing model variant.
- KV cache miss storms were mitigated after shard autoscaling was enabled in Nov 2025.

What we changed (action items completed):
- Revamped alert thresholds and added a delayed paging policy for non-customer-facing errors (Dec 2025).
- Introduced a model-variant health check (Jan 2026) so serving can circuit-break badly performing variants before harming the batcher.
- Implemented automated cache-shard autoscaling and warmup job (Nov 2025).

Open action items (owners and ETA):
- Improve per-model cost dashboards (owner: Jenna Park) — ETA: 2026-03-31.
- Add golden signals regression testing to PR pipelines (owner: Priya Nair) — ETA: 2026-04-15.
- Complete playbook for Dedicated GPU preemption handling (owner: Sanjay Rao) — ETA: 2026-05-01.

6) Roadmap (high-level milestones affecting reliability and runbooks)
Q1 2026 (near-term)
- Multi-region routing: pilot region failover with canary traffic shifting (owner: Leila Gomez) — milestone: cross-region failover test by 2026-02-28.
- Observability retention tiering: enable 90-day high-fidelity traces for SREs (owner: Jenna Park) — milestone: retention policy rollout 2026-03-15.

Q2 2026 (planning)
- Model-variant auto-rollbacks: automatic rollback when per-variant p95 latency regresses > 2x (owner: Priya Nair).
- Cost-aware autoscaling: integrate token-cost signals into scale decisions for Dedicated pools (owner: Sanjay Rao).

7) Platform how-tos & common commands (quick reference)
- Check routing-service p95 latency (Prometheus): copy PromQL from dashboards.
- Roll back a deployment: kubectl -n platform rollout undo deployment/<service> --to-revision=<previous>
- Scale cache shards (one-off): terraform apply -var='shard=<id> scale_delta=+2' — use infra-runbooks to validate change.
- Trigger cache warmup job: kubectl -n platform create job --from=cronjob/cache-warmup cache-warmup-manual-$(date +%s)

8) Attachments and references
- Playbooks: /confluence/eng-platform/platform-systems-services-playbook-2026-q4
- Runbook library: /confluence/eng-platform/platform-systems-services-runbooks-dashboards-roadmap-2026-q3
- oncall rotas and PagerDuty schedules: platform-oncall (internal link)

9) Ownership and escalation contacts
- Platform on-call primary: platform-oncall-primary@redwood.example.com
- Escalation chain: on-call -> service owner -> platform leads -> CTO on-call (only for Sev-1 P0 incidents).

10) Post-incident checklist (required fields for incident ticket)
- Summary, timeline with UTC timestamps, root cause, mitigations applied, affected customers, follow-up actions, owner for each action, ETA.

Notes and style guidance:
- Keep runbooks executable: each step should include a command or dashboard link.
- Avoid pager fatigue: use grouped alerts and delayed paging when possible; reference the delayed paging policy.
- Review owners and SLAs quarterly and after each major deployment.

If you have questions or need edits to this doc, please leave a comment or ping the Platform team channel (#platform-team).
